Hi Samir / Olivia — quick technical responses to your questions: 

1) Rerank API shape: our /v1/rerank endpoint accepts a single request payload that includes the query and an ordered list of candidate documents (we also support batching multiple query objects in one HTTP request). Typical shapes: 
- Single query: {"query": "...", "candidates": [{"id":"doc1", "text":"..."}, ...], "top_k": 5} 
- Batch mode: you can send up to 64 queries in a single request (payload size limits apply). We recommend batching on the client when you evaluate at scale to keep throughput high.

2) Defaults and top_k guidance:
- Retrieval top_k_candidates: 100 is a good starting point for dense retrieval in your domain.
- Reranker top_k (returned items to evaluate): 5 or 10 depending on your UI (we'll evaluate both P@5 and P@10).
- For evaluation, compute metrics across the same cutoff points (P@5, MRR@10, NDCG@10) so you can compare directly.

3) Latency/quality tradeoffs:
- Reranker adds per-query compute; running it on 100 candidates is costlier and slower. Best practice: use retrieval to narrow to ~100 candidates, then rerank the top 20-100 and return top 5. For lower-latency UI endpoints, consider reranker_top_k=10 with aggressive caching of prefix/KV for sessionized queries.

4) Relevance metrics to use for the eval:
- Precision@k (P@5, P@10)
- MRR@10 (captures position bias)
- NDCG@10 (graded relevance if you provide graded labels)
- Failure case sampling: we'll export ~50 low-confidence examples for manual triage.

5) Auth and infra: we can run the eval in Redwood-hosted infra if you upload data to S3 and provide a pre-signed read URL. We will treat the bucket as transient and delete artifacts after the eval window. For production, we recommend a cross-account service role or a customer-managed VPC/private deployment - but that's optional for the PoC.

If you want, I can paste a short SDK snippet for Python showing how to call the rerank endpoint and a batching example.

Perfect — thanks Samir. A few follow-ups and resources attached below: 

- Python SDK snippet (inline):
  - We'll include this in the Drive link but quick example: use client.rerank.batch(queries, batch_size=32, api_key="REDACTED") to send up to 32 queries per HTTP request; each query includes a candidates list.
  - Example heuristics: batch_size=16 for latency-sensitive tests, 32-64 for bulk offline evals.

- Evaluation guidance: NDCG is still useful with mixed labels if you compute it only where graded labels exist; otherwise rely on MRR and P@k for binary labels.
- Thresholding vs fixed top_k: start with fixed top_k in the eval (P@5,P@10,MRR@10). For production, we recommend combining top_k with a score threshold: return items with score > 0.4 OR top_k=5 to avoid empty results. Tune threshold on validation set to control precision/recall tradeoff.
- Hallucination/duplicates: run a cheap near-duplicate filter (min-similarity threshold on embeddings) before reranking; that reduces spurious high scores on near-identical docs.
